boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-cost ways to spend time on or near Oregon State University’s Corvallis campus.

cards.title: Browse Fairbanks Gallery
cards.subtitle: Fairbanks Hall, OSU Corvallis campus
cards.notes: Drop in during the listed weekday hours to look through the current exhibition; check the academic calendar for holiday and term-break closures.
cards.short_summary: A public campus gallery with rotating art displays.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU lists Fairbanks Gallery hours as Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m., and states that it is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Weekday hours are listed as 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; OSU notes holiday and term-break closures.

cards.title: Take the OSU self-guided tour
cards.subtitle: Oregon State University Corvallis campus
cards.notes: Use OSU’s free tour app to choose a route and explore campus at your own pace, following audio stops from student TOUR Ambassadors.
cards.short_summary: A phone-guided campus walk with student-recorded stops.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU says its self-guided tour app is free and can be used on campus for a guided tour experience.
cards.access_notes: Self-guided; use the app and follow normal campus access guidance.

cards.title: Follow the public-art tour
cards.subtitle: OSU Corvallis campus
cards.notes: Download PRAxTours, then make a walk of the campus collection by selecting nearby outdoor works and galleries from the self-guided tour.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided route through OSU’s permanent public art.
cards.evidence_claim: PRAx states that PRAxTours offers self-guided tours of campus public art, galleries, and the visual and performing arts center.
cards.source_title: Public Art | PRAx | Oregon State University
cards.access_notes: Self-guided via the PRAxTours mobile app; outdoor works can be viewed while campus areas are accessible.

cards.title: Meet on the MU Quad
cards.subtitle: 2501 SW Jefferson Way, Corvallis
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or a Frisbee and use the open lawn between the Memorial Union and Milam Hall for a low-key outdoor meetup.
cards.short_summary: A central campus lawn for casual outdoor time.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU identifies the Memorial Union Quad as a large open space between the Memorial Union and Milam Hall; OSU also states that Frisbees, yard games, and picnics are welcome on campus lawns.
cards.source_title: How to get the most out of OSU green spaces
cards.access_notes: Campus is open to the public; avoid reserved areas or events and follow posted site guidance.

cards.entity_name: Oak Creek Center for Urban Horticulture
cards.title: Walk Oak Creek’s gardens
cards.subtitle: 844 SW 35th St., Corvallis
cards.notes: Take a daylight loop through the horticulture center and slow down around the habitat plantings; use the walk-around gate access if it is closed.
cards.short_summary: A campus-edge garden and wildlife habitat open daily.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU Extension states that the Oak Creek Center for Urban Horticulture is open to the public from dawn to dusk and visitors may walk around a closed gate.
cards.source_title: Oak Creek Center for Urban Horticulture designated a Certified Wildlife Habitat
cards.access_notes: Open to the public dawn to dusk; the source says visitors may walk around a closed gate.

cards.title: Walk the Avery Park loop
cards.subtitle: Avery Park and Natural Area, 1200 SW Avery Park Dr.
cards.notes: Use the one-mile walking and jogging trail for a conversation-paced lap, then pause by the Marys River riparian area before heading back.
cards.short_summary: A one-mile park loop alongside the Marys River.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Corvallis describes a one-mile walking/jogging trail through Avery Park and along the Marys River riparian area.
cards.source_title: Avery Park and Natural Area | Corvallis Oregon
cards.access_notes: Use public park paths; picnic shelters may be reserved for private events, so do not use a reserved shelter.

cards.title: Wander the Rose Garden
cards.subtitle: Avery Park and Natural Area, near the northwest entrance
cards.notes: Walk the garden’s paths and benches during the May–October bloom season; leave every bloom and fallen petal in place for other visitors.
cards.short_summary: A public rose garden with arbors, benches, art, and paths.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says the Rose Garden has benches, arbors, art, and trails, and its rules apply to both renters and the general public.
cards.access_notes: General-public access is described; do not clip or collect roses or petals, and yield to permitted private events.

cards.title: Hike Chip Ross
cards.subtitle: Chip Ross Park and Natural Area, Lester Avenue access
cards.notes: Start at the Lester Avenue trailhead and take the easy-to-moderate 1.5-mile loop; bring water and stay on the established trail.
cards.short_summary: A short oak-woodland hike with hilltop views.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Corvallis describes an easy-to-moderate 1.5-mile hiking trail at Chip Ross Natural Area and identifies Lester Avenue parking access.
cards.source_title: Chip Ross Park and Natural Area | Corvallis Oregon
cards.access_notes: Access is at the end of Lester Avenue; use designated trails and observe posted seasonal trail rules.

cards.entity_name: Forest Discovery Trail at Peavy Arboretum
cards.title: Explore Peavy’s Forest Discovery Trail
cards.subtitle: Peavy Arboretum, 7 miles north of Corvallis
cards.notes: Pick up the self-guided materials and follow the 1.2-mile forest hike from Arboretum Parking, using the prompts to notice ecology and history.
cards.short_summary: A guided, hands-on forest walk at Peavy Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: OSU’s Forest Discovery Trail guide states that the program is free to use for OSU Research Forest visitors and takes place at Peavy Arboretum.
cards.source_title: Forest Discovery Trail Program Teacher’s Guide
cards.access_notes: The trail begins from Arboretum Parking; plan for a 1.2-mile outdoor hike and check local conditions before leaving.

cards.title: Take a downtown Central Park break
cards.subtitle: 650 NW Monroe Ave., Corvallis
cards.notes: Use the paved walkways, benches, playground, and sculpture stops for a relaxed downtown reset; leave dogs at home because they are not allowed here.
cards.short_summary: A downtown park with walkways, public art, benches, and a playground.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Corvallis describes Central Park as a public downtown park with paved walkways, sculptures, resting benches, and a playground.
cards.access_notes: City page lists the park at 650 NW Monroe Avenue and says dogs are not allowed.
